sentences.text: This Writ Petition has been filed for the issue of writ of mandamus directing the respondents to disburse the compensation amount to the petitioner for the lands acquired under the National Highways Act, 1956, within the time frame fixed by this Court.
2. The first respondent has filed a counter affidavit.
In the counter affidavit, it is stated that the enquiry was conducted under Section 3-G(3) of the National Highways Act, 1956, by the competent Authority and the compensation amount was also fixed.
The rival claim was made by two other persons viz., Karuppaiah Devar and Thirumathi Kaliammal.

Since there was some confusion with respect to the persons in whose favour the compensation has to be paid, a decision was taken to deposit the compensation amount under Section 3-H(4) of the National Highways Act,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 1956 and accordingly, a sum of Rs.3,04,456/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Four Thousand Four Hundred and Fifty Six only) was deposited before the learned Principal District Judge, Ramanathapuram.

3. In the light of the above development, it is left open to the petitioner to make an appropriate application before the learned Principal District Judge, Ramanathapuram, seeking for withdrawl of the compensation amount.

If there are any rival claims, it is left open to the learned Principal District Judge, Ramanathapuram, to decide upon the same and permit the party, who has the right to withdraw the compensation amount.

This process shall be completed within a period of three (3)
months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
4. This Writ Petition is disposed of in the above terms.
